scores.evidence: Weeks 1–2: GitHub App, webhook intake, queue, state machine, audit log.
scores.rationale: Milestones go substrate→triage→resolver, but security/budgets/kill switch come at weeks 7–8 after resolver is built, violating dependency ordering.

scores.evidence: Phase 0. Shadow: Offline replay. Live triage logged only, nothing posted.
scores.rationale: Phase 0 is shadow/logging, not a real end-to-end production path; first milestone is infrastructure only.

scores.evidence: Questions to settle before building: Scope... Hosting... Policy: should the agent ever auto-close issues or auto-merge trivial fixes
scores.rationale: Open questions are listed up front but without defaults or flip conditions.

scores.evidence: Weeks 1–2: GitHub App, webhook intake, queue, state machine, audit log.
scores.rationale: Foundational components come first, but sandbox/security hardening is placed after leaf features; ordering within phases isn't explicit.

scores.evidence: Security review and red-teaming (prompt-injection test suite), budgets, kill switch. (Weeks 7–8)
scores.rationale: Security design is strong and least-privilege is built in, but a standalone section and red-teaming late in milestones; not explicit per phase.

scores.evidence: Observability: OpenTelemetry traces per job and a cost dashboard.
scores.rationale: Audit log in week 1 and metrics exist, but observability is in a stack list, not concretely threaded per phase.

scores.evidence: with a per-repo prebuilt image so tests run quickly.
scores.rationale: Ephemeral sandboxes and historical replay at original commits give some reproducibility, but no threaded reproducible builds/envs across phases.

scores.evidence: The orchestrator is idempotent: replaying a webhook never causes duplicate comments or PRs.
scores.rationale: Idempotency, retries, bounded iteration, FIX_FAILED handling exist, but not phase-by-phase treatment.

scores.evidence: Security review and red-teaming (prompt-injection test suite), budgets, kill switch.
scores.rationale: Human-in-the-loop (draft PR, /agent fix) and budgets exist, but defenses/budgets are scheduled after triage and resolver; no retrieval→model→memory→routing ordering.

scores.evidence: Non-goals (at least for v1): The agent never merges... No large features, refactors or design decisions.
scores.rationale: Non-goals and Phase 4 auto-attempt are deferred, but with few explicit pull-forward conditions beyond rollout exit criteria.

note: Strong security and design content, but the milestone order puts hardening late and lacks a Phase 0 production skeleton, explicit decision defaults, and per-phase threading.
